new_from_file.brief: Creates a new `GtkImage` displaying the file `filename`.
new_from_file.md:
Creates a new `GtkImage` displaying the file `filename`.

If the file isn’t found or can’t be loaded, the resulting `GtkImage`
will display a “broken image” icon. This function never returns `NULL`,
it always returns a valid `GtkImage` widget.

If you need to detect failures to load the file, use an
image loading framework such as libglycin to load the file
yourself, then create the `GtkImage` from the texture.

The storage type (see [`Image.get_storage_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:get_storage_type))
of the returned image is not defined, it will be whatever
is appropriate for displaying the file.

new_from_gicon.brief: Creates a `GtkImage` displaying an icon from the current icon theme.
new_from_gicon.md:
Creates a `GtkImage` displaying an icon from the current icon theme.

If the icon name isn’t known, a “broken image” icon will be
displayed instead. If the current icon theme is changed, the icon
will be updated appropriately.

new_from_icon_name.brief: Creates a `GtkImage` displaying an icon from the current icon theme.
new_from_icon_name.md:
Creates a `GtkImage` displaying an icon from the current icon theme.

If the icon name isn’t known, a “broken image” icon will be
displayed instead. If the current icon theme is changed, the icon
will be updated appropriately.

new_from_paintable.md:
Creates a new `GtkImage` displaying `paintable`.

The `GtkImage` does not assume a reference to the paintable; you still
need to unref it if you own references. `GtkImage` will add its own
reference rather than adopting yours.

The `GtkImage` will track changes to the `paintable` and update
its size and contents in response to it.

Note that paintables are still subject to the icon size that is
set on the image. If you want to display a paintable at its intrinsic
size, use [`Picture`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture) instead.

If `paintable` is a [`SymbolicPaintable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SymbolicPaintable), then it will be
recolored with the symbolic palette from the theme.

new_from_pixbuf.md:
Creates a new `GtkImage` displaying `pixbuf`.

The `GtkImage` does not assume a reference to the pixbuf; you still
need to unref it if you own references. `GtkImage` will add its own
reference rather than adopting yours.

This is a helper for [`Image.new_from_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_paintable), and you can't
get back the exact pixbuf once this is called, only a texture.

Note that this function just creates an `GtkImage` from the pixbuf.
The `GtkImage` created will not react to state changes. Should you
want that, you should use [`Image.new_from_icon_name()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_icon_name).

new_from_resource.brief: Creates a new `GtkImage` displaying the resource file `resource_path`.
new_from_resource.md:
Creates a new `GtkImage` displaying the resource file `resource_path`.

If the file isn’t found or can’t be loaded, the resulting `GtkImage` will
display a “broken image” icon. This function never returns `NULL`,
it always returns a valid `GtkImage` widget.

If you need to detect failures to load the file, use an
image loading framework such as libglycin to load the file
yourself, then create the `GtkImage` from the texture.

The storage type (see [`Image.get_storage_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:get_storage_type)) of
the returned image is not defined, it will be whatever is
appropriate for displaying the file.

doc.md:
Displays an image.

Various kinds of object can be displayed as an image; most typically,
you would load a `GdkTexture` from a file, using the convenience function
[`Image.new_from_file()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_file), for instance:

```c
GtkWidget *image = gtk_image_new_from_file ("myfile.png");
```

If the file isn’t loaded successfully, the image will contain a
“broken image” icon similar to that used in many web browsers.

If you want to handle errors in loading the file yourself, for example
by displaying an error message, then load the image with an image
loading framework such as libglycin, then create the `GtkImage` with
[`Image.new_from_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_paintable).

Sometimes an application will want to avoid depending on external data
files, such as image files. See the documentation of `GResource` inside
GIO, for details. In this case, [`Image:resource`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#property:resource),
[`Image.new_from_resource()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_resource), and [`Image.set_from_resource()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:set_from_resource)
should be used.

`GtkImage` displays its image as an icon, with a size that is determined
by the application. See [`Picture`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Picture) if you want to show an image
at is actual size.

## CSS nodes

`GtkImage` has a single CSS node with the name `image`. The style classes
`.normal-icons` or `.large-icons` may appear, depending on the
[`Image:icon-size`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#property:icon-size) property.

## Accessibility

`GtkImage` uses the [`AccessibleRole.img`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:img) role.

clear.brief: Resets the image to be empty.
clear.md: Resets the image to be empty.

get_gicon.brief: Gets the `GIcon` being displayed by the `GtkImage`.
get_gicon.md:
Gets the `GIcon` being displayed by the `GtkImage`.

The storage type of the image must be %GTK_IMAGE_EMPTY or
%GTK_IMAGE_GICON (see [`Image.get_storage_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:get_storage_type)).
The caller of this function does not own a reference to the
returned `GIcon`.

get_icon_name.brief: Gets the icon name and size being displayed by the `GtkImage`.
get_icon_name.md:
Gets the icon name and size being displayed by the `GtkImage`.

The storage type of the image must be %GTK_IMAGE_EMPTY or
%GTK_IMAGE_ICON_NAME (see [`Image.get_storage_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:get_storage_type)).
The returned string is owned by the `GtkImage` and should not
be freed.

get_icon_size.brief: Gets the icon size used by the `image` when rendering icons.
get_icon_size.md: Gets the icon size used by the `image` when rendering icons.

get_paintable.brief: Gets the image `GdkPaintable` being displayed by the `GtkImage`.
get_paintable.md:
Gets the image `GdkPaintable` being displayed by the `GtkImage`.

The storage type of the image must be %GTK_IMAGE_EMPTY or
%GTK_IMAGE_PAINTABLE (see [`Image.get_storage_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:get_storage_type)).
The caller of this function does not own a reference to the
returned paintable.

get_pixel_size.brief: Gets the pixel size used for named icons.
get_pixel_size.md: Gets the pixel size used for named icons.

get_storage_type.brief: Gets the type of representation being used by the `GtkImage` to store image data.
get_storage_type.md:
Gets the type of representation being used by the `GtkImage`
to store image data.

If the `GtkImage` has no image data, the return value will
be %GTK_IMAGE_EMPTY.

set_from_file.brief: Sets a `GtkImage` to show a file.
set_from_file.md:
Sets a `GtkImage` to show a file.

See [`Image.new_from_file()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_file) for details.

::: warning
    Note that this function should not be used with untrusted data.
    Use a proper image loading framework such as libglycin, which can
    load many image formats into a `GdkTexture`, and then use
    [`Image.set_from_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:set_from_paintable).

set_from_gicon.md:
Sets a `GtkImage` to show a `GIcon`.

See [`Image.new_from_gicon()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_gicon) for details.

set_from_icon_name.brief: Sets a `GtkImage` to show a named icon.
set_from_icon_name.md:
Sets a `GtkImage` to show a named icon.

See [`Image.new_from_icon_name()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_icon_name) for details.

set_from_paintable.md:
Sets a `GtkImage` to show a `GdkPaintable`.

See [`Image.new_from_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_paintable) for details.

set_from_pixbuf.md:
Sets a `GtkImage` to show a `GdkPixbuf`.

See [`Image.new_from_pixbuf()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_pixbuf) for details.

Note: This is a helper for [`Image.set_from_paintable()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:set_from_paintable),
and you can't get back the exact pixbuf once this is called,
only a paintable.

set_from_resource.brief: Sets a `GtkImage` to show a resource.
set_from_resource.md:
Sets a `GtkImage` to show a resource.

See [`Image.new_from_resource()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#constructor:new_from_resource) for details.

set_icon_size.brief: Suggests an icon size to the theme for named icons.
set_icon_size.md: Suggests an icon size to the theme for named icons.

set_pixel_size.brief: Sets the pixel size to use for named icons.
set_pixel_size.md:
Sets the pixel size to use for named icons.

If the pixel size is set to a value != -1, it is used instead
of the icon size set by [`Image.set_icon_size()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#method:set_icon_size).

file.brief: A path to the file to display.
file.md: A path to the file to display.

gicon.md:
The `GIcon` displayed in the GtkImage.

For themed icons, If the icon theme is changed, the image will be updated
automatically.

icon-name.brief: The name of the icon in the icon theme.
icon-name.md:
The name of the icon in the icon theme.

If the icon theme is changed, the image will be updated automatically.

icon-size.brief: The symbolic size to display icons at.
icon-size.md: The symbolic size to display icons at.

pixel-size.brief: The size in pixels to display icons at.
pixel-size.md:
The size in pixels to display icons at.

If set to a value != -1, this property overrides the
[`Image:icon-size`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Image#property:icon-size) property for images of type
`GTK_IMAGE_ICON_NAME`.

resource.brief: A path to a resource file to display.
resource.md: A path to a resource file to display.

storage-type.brief: The representation being used for image data.
storage-type.md: The representation being used for image data.

use-fallback.brief: Whether the icon displayed in the `GtkImage` will use standard icon names fallback.
use-fallback.md:
Whether the icon displayed in the `GtkImage` will use
standard icon names fallback.

The value of this property is only relevant for images of type
%GTK_IMAGE_ICON_NAME and %GTK_IMAGE_GICON.
